target_customer: Pharma partners and investors who fund drug programs against transcription factors; early revenue came from collaborations
problem: Transcription factors drive disease but are considered undruggable. Arpeggio used RNA sequencing time series and machine learning to find compounds that modulate them.
business_model: Biotech drug discovery with collaboration revenue and venture funded pipeline

founders.name: Joey Azofeifa
education: CU Boulder (IQ Biology program alum, per university news)
founders.background_notes: Named to the 2020 Forbes 30 Under 30 in Healthcare per the January 2020 press release title.

founders.name: Robin Dowell
founders.background_notes: CU Boulder venture partners page (via search) says the company was founded in 2017 by Azofeifa and Dowell. Not on the YC page.

exit.reason: Fierce Biotech headline says the company disbanded on poor prospects for its Nrf2 program, with the CEO saying the program had begun to unravel

technical_complexity.rationale: Drugging transcription factors with a new RNA sequencing and machine learning approach is research grade and needs wet lab, data and chemistry.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary time series transcriptome data and a platform validated by partners, but drug programs still face standard biotech clinical risk.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer emerged. FORMA Therapeutics collaborated with Arpeggio in March 2018 per its press release and the company reported J and J as a partner.

market_need_then: Transcription factors were a large class of disease targets seen as undruggable. FORMA announced a collaboration in March 2018 to use the platform to analyze biological effects of drug candidates.

branding.domain_note: Uses arpeggiobio.com. Earlier legal name Arpeggio Biosciences, shortened to Arpeggio Bio.

identity.logo: Refreshed identity built with design agency Wunderdogs per a Webflow case study
identity.visual_style: Brand refresh with new visual identity and website

rebrands.why: A brand refresh with Wunderdogs is described, reasons not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Press used musical wordplay when it shut down (Fierce Biotech headline).

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage of funding and the closure, but no evidence the brand helped partnering or hiring.

outcome_analysis: Arpeggio raised a 3.2 million dollar seed in January 2020 and a 17 million dollar Series A in September 2022, reaching about 20 million dollars in total. It partnered with FORMA from 2018 and later J and J. Its lead Nrf2 program ran into trouble and trade press and CU Boulder reported the company disbanding around August 2026 after about eight years. The cause is a failing lead drug program, a technical biology risk rather than a market problem.
notes: The YC directory still lists the company as Active but the Fierce Biotech headline and the CU Boulder page (both seen via search results; Fierce page itself returned 403) report a wind down in August 2026, so exit is recorded as shutdown. A single aggregator says the CEO announced it in July 2026. The seed investor list is taken from the Series A coverage describing existing seed backers (Khosla, TechU, FundersClub, Alice Zhang, Fifty Years) and a seed press summary naming Y Combinator; the seed press release page returned 403. Series A and total over 20 million dollars from BioSpace, MedCity News and Business Wire via search. Company website returned 404. Competitors named on one undated profile (Talus Bio, Sanofi, Nurix) were not dated near 2019, so none are listed. Founding year differs (2017 CU page, 2018 press release).
